item.title: Re: The Shield that Redirects its Damage
item.content:encoded:
Hello HelloThere! let's take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A viking shield that when held by a living person will cause a blue energy field to cover it. The energy field can redirect any damage that is inflicted upon it right back at the attacker (Examples: Shooting it with a gun will result in bullet wounds appearing in you or slashing at it with a sharp weapon will give you stab wounds and cuts). However, it does have its limits.

Overall, the skip feels like a "thing that does a thing", as the object doesn't seem to have much of purpose or origin. The main focus from both the narrative and concept seem to be the effects, which currently fall fairly flat, as there isn't anything beyond "shield that deflects attacks". What about this will make me as the reader invested? is there any sort of history behind the skip? whats its purpose? how do its effects relate to that purpose?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The shield was discovered in Norway in a viking ship burial by some archaeologists. The SCP came to the foundation's attention when reports of a cursed and powerful shield erupted upon its discovery so an investigation was initiated and the SCP was recovered. Tests and experiments were conducted to understand how it works which usually consisted of D-Class personnel and weaponized machinery attacking it.

While there is a setup here, a strong middle act and payoff are missing. The story isn't building up to anything, or showing much other than "Foundation finds and then tests something". The tests alone won't be able to carry the story, as they don't offer anything to really get invested in.

Along with this the narrative is missing a conflict. All of the events go off without a hitch and the Foundation doesn't have any sort of reason of care about the skip, which makes the story feel a bit flat and unnatural.

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is unknown where the shield gained its anomalous ability and who the creator/original wielder was. There is also little information on how the SCP generates its blue energy field though it is possible that there is some sort of mystical or magical force surrounding it.

This feels like a quick/lazy way to explain the skips effects and origin, especially with the lack of other main focuses (the Foundation is only testing the skips effects) in the narrative or concept.

The shield could provide potential use to the foundation, but if fallen into the wrong hands it could lead to many problems.

I would recommend you look at making this more apparent in the narrative (from what I can see this barely gets mention in the story). Show how this would be useful, why it's dangerous in the wrong hands, what would happen ect.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

Recommendations:
-My main issue is the lack of a strong conflict and payoff in the narrative, there isn't much to really get invested in. - I would recommend expanding upon possible ideas for conflict or exploitation. (the Foundation using it for their own gain, other parties trying to steal it, ect.)

-the skip itself only really shows its effects, which alone aren't interesting enough to carry the article. - I wold recommend you get a rough idea of the origin and purpose of the skip, as developing it fully, will allow you to pick and choose what is and isn't necessary to include. (it can also help with developing the narrative!)

- the plot line feels unfinished due to the lack of a strong payoff. - Show something more than just tests, what does everything build up to? why are they testing it? what is learnt by the end? ect.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: Ever Upwards
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Existential thriller, mystery

Elevator Pitch:
+ Elevator Pitch
- Elevator Pitch

This scp is, in a sense, humanity's seeming desire to leave earth's atmosphere and explore outer space. This scp was discovered once the foundation began to notice strange patterns in the direction and movement of every human and manmade object launched into space, as well as every other object in space (planets, stars, etc), which all appear to be converging to an unknown spot in spacetime at irregular speeds.

Central Narrative:
+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

While investigating several other space related anomalies, the foundation begins to put together a strange pattern in the movement of every object that has been launched into space, which all eventually begin to travel in the same exact direction. Digging further, they find a cut section of the Apollo 11 landing, during which mike collins seems to jump and be dragged out in this exact same direction for a few seconds, contrary to the observed gravitational effects of the moon. Curiously, satelites in orbit around earth such as the ISS are unaffected, as well as celestial bodies such as the planets, moons, and sun. However, calculations run by the foundation indicate that these bodies only appear to be unaffected, and have actually been moving in an even pace to one another in this direction for a while. Finally, the foundation uncovers that, over the course of millenia, every object in the universe has been traveling towards a single undefined point in space.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
+ Hook/Attention Grabber
- Hook/Attention Grabber

After running some tests, the foundation manages to calculate the coordinates for this point. After a predictably long journey, they finally manage to send a ship to the coordinates, which finds a barely describable fold in spacetime where all things are seemingly erased. Ordered to return, the unmanned ship curiously defies its controls and moves towards the fold, and strong radio interference is heard as the ship displays a white void. The foundation finds the sounds to be their only lead, and work to decipher a potential meaning. Although they fail, an incident occurs where these sounds are heard again from the sky, this time being mysteriously comprehensible, with the message:
"You have protected your world
from a great many threats,
from those which are incomprehensible,
and for that I am proud.
But what comes now you are not prepared for,
nor am I,
so I must protect you now,
within my unwavering.
Join me,
In this void,
and travel ever upward,
for you have no other choice"

The article ends with a question: If after all the foundation has fought, this void only interferes now, then what exactly is coming for us?

Additional Notes: Hope this isn't too similar to anything else and that it's interesting!

item.title: Individual Rating Modules for Log Entries
item.content:encoded:
Low-quality content naturally piles up in places like 682's termination log, 1459's extended logs, and other very large collaborative lists. Inevitably, a page curator has to go through and prune away the bad entries. I imagine that this is tiresome and time-consuming for the curator, and it also means that garbage entries in these logs live much longer than an equally garbage SCP would. If there were some way to install individual rating modules for each item on the log, so they could be voted on individually, then perhaps that might save some time for the curator and shorten the lifespan of the bad entries.

I thought that the log of extranormal events or unexplained locations was already like this, but it seems that I was mistaken.

item.title: Seeking Critique (Love Potion No. 9)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Elevator Pitch: This is an SCP based upon the narrative created by the song, Love Potion No. 9, made popular by The Clovers in 1959. The premise is that the SCP is the actual love potion described in the song, more or less. The object itself is a safe object, characterized as being an opaque black liquid contained within a small glass bottle. The liquid itself is described as smelling of turpentine. Its anomalous property is that it causes the drinker to lose all romantic and sexual discretion, except for a marked increase in the attractiveness of members of law enforcement.

Central Narrative: This object came to the attention of the Foundation after a young man was arrested and brought to a mental asylum after falling under the effects of the love potion and succeeding in his attempt to passionately kiss a police officer on patrol. The young man informed officials that he was compelled to behave in that manner after drinking a potion, created by a gypsy fortune teller named Madame Ruth in order to cure him of his bad luck with women.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is an SCP based on a well known piece of pop culture history. I feel like people will find it quite amusing and maybe even humorous.

Additional Notes: I hope you guys see this as a lighthearted, humorous attempt at an SCP article.

item.content:encoded:
The following logs have been pruned from the log:

+ Pruned logs
– hide block

Unexplained Location UE-655588
Description: A small communal, Christian church marked in city records as "the West Tennesse Peoples Church of Churchism", shown to be entirely constructed of organic matter. The only other feature of note surrounding UE-655588 is that the object was formerly Pastor Henry Ecclesia, who slowly transformed into the church between 1970 and 1971.
Date of Containment: 1971-03-12
Location: Outside Clarksville, Tennesse.
Security Protocol: The church is to be patrolled by two guards, under the cover story of Asbestos Cleanup operations. All individuals who enter the church are to be removed. Any individuals who discover the objects anomalous properties are to be provided with Class-A amnestics.
Note: A small plaque was found engraved on the southwestern flank of the structure, transcribed below:

TO THE GLORY OF GOD 1971:

THIS CHURCH WAS MADE OF AND BY PASTOR HENRY ECCLESIA. HIS SACRIFICE TO BECOME ONE WITH THE LORD AND HIS FOLLOWERS WILL NEVER BE FORGOTTEN. HIS BLOOD, SWEAT, TEARS, ORGANS, SKIN, AND MUSCLES WERE USED TO BUILD A HOME FOR OUR LORD AND HIS SUN. [sic]

”Those who wish to be a church can be under God, for that is his way.” - Jesus Christ (Assumed).

Unexplained Location UE-96843
Description: A small Victorian Era house originally owned by 'Sir Oswald Francis', a tea-trader from the United Kingdom. When the attic door is opened, it will lead to an extradimensional location roughly resembling a massive tea plantation. In the centre of the plantation is a large factory complex. Every individual who enters the pocket dimension will simultaneously appear in both the attic entrance (which leads to a small shack) and the factory. They will also feel an impossible compulsion to harvest tea from the plantation and put the leaves on a pully within the structure, and then to place a weight on the other pully. The individual who moves out of the factory will be unable to exit the dimension, whereas the individuals who enter via the attic entrance will be able to exit. Several notable individuals are within the structure including, but not limited to, George Washington, Winston Churchill, Queen Elizabeth II, Sir Oswald Francis, Kristina Francis, every member of the beetles, and 83 duplicates of an unidentified worker.
Date of Containment: Since Foundation Inception.
Location: Ganges Delta, Bangladesh.
Security Protocol: Two guards stationed around the structure. Produced tea checked for anomalies and sold as a part of Sir Conrod Products (an SCP foundation front company.)

Unexplained Location UE-39221
Description: Roughly 204 billion exoplanets 189 billion light-years from Earth, with several anomalous effects. The planets exist within the radius of each other where gravitational action would result in their destruction, and move in erratic and impossible patterns. The planets, when viewed through a satellite, resemble 21 tangled double-helix structures forming into large structures. Despite these structures large mass, no gravitational effects occur on nearby planets. The double helix structure of this planetary system is sometimes threaded through large masses of planets, which somehow causes a single helix structure to move from this mass, flip, and then thread itself together with another double helix structure.
When the atmospheric composition and sizes of these planets are accounted for, the planets can be assigned to several elements from the periodic table. Using this model, the planetary structure has been found to be an exact match to the genome of a human male, with 16% Irish heritage, 53% Indian heritage, 30.2% English descent and 0.2% from other locations. The individual is known to have blue eyes, red hair, and pale white skin. So far no exact genetic match for this has been found.

Date of Containment: 2014-05-12, After discovery by foundation FTL probe.
Location: Galaxy supercluster XY-539222.
Security Protocol: It is unlikely that UE-39221 will ever be discovered, due to extreme distances from the earth, and as such, no security protocol is needed.

All of these logs were pruned for length — entries to this list should be of relatively short length, and not extensively detailed.

You did a really good job putting personality in all of the characters. I Loved the jokes and the dialogue as well. Easy +1.

I only have two critiques, but they're minor (get it). First is a grammatical error. In the first part of addendum 1, you wrote "D-060173 was tethered and given an heat-proof armor, oxygen tank, and night-vision goggles." It should be "D-060173 was tethered and given an heat-proof armor, an oxygen tank, and night-vision goggles."

Secondly is that at the end of the description, you included the sentence "The exact nature of SCP-5594 is unknown and an investigation is ongoing". I don't think that sentence makes much sense for two reasons. Firstly, that paragraph was pretty specific in describing the effects and entities of the scp, so it felt weird for you to say it wasn't fully understood. In the context of the article as a whole it makes even less sense, since there isn't exactly any mystery as to what's going on by the end.

Other than that, it was a very fun read

item.title: Re: What are your unusual headcanons?
item.content:encoded:
Demotion to D-Class and Keter duty are not real things, they're stories made up to mess with new recruits/scare them into being careful. Likewise, monthly termination is something that more experienced D-class tell the new guys as a form of hazing. These ridiculous things show up in official documentation because sometimes the files are being written by newbies who haven't yet learned that there's no such thing.

Alternatively, the higher-ups want people to believe that demotion to D and Keter duty exist because it keeps them in line. They really do put things like that in the documentation to threaten people, and even though it never actually happens there are still people who believe it's possible. The only way to find out for sure would be to dump some 447 on a dead body and see if you get demoted to D or not (assuming that you survive, of course), and nobody's stupid or crazy enough to try that.

item.title: Re: ClicheFinder™
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open
[-] Close

Here's some crit:

the said subject would then be ignored for 2 hours, to 508 days.

This is a bit unclear: does this make other people ignore whatever the subject is, or does it make the subject not be affectable by SCP-XXXX for up to 508 days?

Class-D wrote himself on the paper, the subject was deemed "rare" and no other effect commenced.

This is simply my opinion, but this is… Boring? I feel there should be some narrative shown here, perhaps unfolding how the SCP rates the "cliché-ness" of things? Because as it stands, this D-Class was labeled "rare" for no reason at all.

Researcher wrote "Dr. Bright" on paper

This kind of thing belongs in the lolfoundation and would not happen in the professional environment of the Foundation, despite what your headcanon may say.

Researcher entered "Procedure 110-Montauk"

I believe it would be unwise to casually mention one of the most commonly known things on the site next to a [DATA EXPUNGED] sign.

got this idea from reading a ton of SCP's and got pissed from the clichés.

From the way this concept post is written, I think you have read many Series I SCP's and are taking a lot of inspiration from the shallowness of that time. Work on the story that is being told over the course of the article and what it truly means to be cliché. If there is no reason for the subject to age 34 years, don't have them age 34 years, same thing goes for, "3 hours and 34 minutes" and, "0.23 seconds to 246 days." If it doesn't work into the story it's fluff and you should cut it out of the article.

The pitch comes off as bland and storyless with a lot of fluff and unprofessionalism from the Foundation.

item.title: Re: No Happy Endings

The idea is kind of a darker spin on a Disney movie/Fairy tale, where the big bad godmother does some magic spell to usurp the kingdom, but instead of the knight in shining armour coming along and helping save the day, the foundation contains the magically altered princess and the queen is never defeated. The reason West Trancidentalia sounds made up is that it is meant to be a kind of 'fairy tale land', and the diplomat is meant to be some shill who tried to smuggle the princess out of that place. Then the final song is '/I can't go back home, ever!/' because if she does, she'll be destroyed. I'll make the edits now.

item.title: Re: Time: Limited
item.content:encoded:
This collapsible will contain an updated and more in-depth version of the concept.

Massive edit:

Lots of text
Sorry for wall of text

The signals reveal that the canis major dwarf galaxy has been in indefinite quarantine for about a millennia. With the alien race having spent this time keeping the mass from breaching containment and exiting the galaxy.

Further information is received a year later, telling of the origin of the mass. At some point, a signal was triggered by an experimental technology which resulted in a change in the genetic code of 30% of the alien race. This change resulted in the rapid generation of sentient cells that act as a hive mind, think cancer if it had a sense of self. The affected individuals quickly became overwhelmed by the cancerous cells, eventually being entirely consumed. The separate smaller masses sought out one another to grow, as they grew in size, they similarly grew in intellect.

Another year passes before another signal is received (this will be a yearly pattern). The sender expresses immense remorse before divulging information relating to damaging the mass, or at least holding it off. The leaders of the alien species performed many experiments, some far less ethical than others. The spinal fluid of approximately 8% of individuals that die in their sleep contains an anomalous chemical that tears apart the mass on the molecular level. However, the aliens are unsure as to whether or not other species have this same chemical.
In an attempt to neutralise the mass, 50 kilolitres of spinal fluid containing the chemical is dropped onto it. The mass essentially begins melting and makes a direct B line to a megacity on the species home planet. Attempts to stop it are unsuccessful and the mass regenerates. After this, it enters orbit by literally launching itself into space. It adapts to the inhospitable conditions near instantaneously, floating from planet to planet, consuming all life it comes across. A total of 50% of the population had been lost due to the increase in aggression of the mass.

A final effort to prevent the mass from ending the civilisation was made, where a planet the mass had just landed at is encased in a metal alloy. The mass is constantly weakened by continuous railgun fire.
Due to a jam that prevented railgun fire for 20 seconds, the mass was able to tear its containment unit to shreds along with the railgun stations. At this point, the mass had grown sufficiently enough to communicate although in a rudimentary way. It emits a soundwave, saying, “Scaring. Leave.”

The alien race dedicates the rest of its existence to reversing what they believe is their mistake, constantly engaging with the mass and preventing it from leaving the galaxy.
Eventually, the mass adapts, emitting a heatwave that spans the entire galaxy. This heatwave has two effects: Burning any living being to death due to its temperature exceeding 1000 degrees Celsius. Secondly, it converts those exposed into separate instances of the mass, which seek out each other and join the main mass.

The last remnants of the alien race; those housed in underground government facilities, are the ones that sent out the signals. The final signal tells of these last remaining aliens, and how they are sorry for the responsibility that has been placed on the surrounding galaxies.
As the mass reaches 5000 lightyears from earth, it sends out its own signals, which contain a LOT of binary. The translated signals are oddly friendly, stating that it will not bring harm and that it is tired.

Communication is established and the foundation conducts a series of interviews by sending out questions in binary and translating the response. The mass talks of its origin, stating that it does not know how it came to be, only that there was darkness then there was light. It was a child, hungry and afraid, but it is older now and understands that eating causes death. It says that it met a being of machine and flesh, which told the mass a “beautiful message”. The mass has refused to eat since it received the message, choosing to observe and learn. Because it has been starving itself, it is dying. It saw earth and its natural wonders and felt that earth would be a nice final destination. The problem is, of course, that the foundation has been given a very gruesome depiction of this mass, and a large mass of flesh that wiped out an entire civilisation is the easiest to trust.

Essentially, an alien civilisation was wiped out by an eldritch abomination that developed due to their use of experimental technology. They sent out a series of messages to explain what happened, and what threat has been unleashed. The foundation is left with a dilemma though. After the mass expresses a desire to not bring harm but rather to have a peaceful death, the foundation is left having to decide what to trust. Additionally, the mass references "others" in the surrounding galaxies, giving a rather grim reason for why we haven't seen much alien life.

I am also considering having the mass speak of a "father", which will involve some references to Yaldabaoth as a possible reason for the creation of the mass.

item.title: ClicheFinder™
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article (ACS)

Genre: meta

Elevator Pitch:

An unbranded notebook. When a description, name, or information is written on the 57th page of the notebook, the notebook then proceeds to display the "cliche-ness" of such information. The basing of this "cliche-ness" is unknown, and no reasonable pattern has been reported". Guidelines if whether the subjects is a cliche:

  • If the subject is a person, the said subject would then lose consciousness for approximately 3 hours and 34 minutes. After this effect, the subject loses all memories of the incident.
  • If the subject is an object (or tangible principle), the subject would then disappear from reality from the range of 0.23 seconds to 246 days. The object would then seemed to have aged 34 years whether it disappeared for any of the specified range of time.
+ show block
– hide block
  • If the subject is a description, the notebook would then identify the described object and classify it to its "cliche-ness". The object would have an effect similar to that of the previous.
  • If the subject is a name for a process, protocol, or any executable procedure, the said subject would then be ignored for 2 hours, to 508 days. This is to NOT be attempted, for any foundation protocol or procedure is to be kept ongoing for eternity.
  • If the subject is a natural law or simply an "unchangeable principle", the subject would experience no other effects that would commence.

Note: If the subject is an extreme cliche, the effects amplify.
LOG:

  • Class-D wrote himself on the paper, the subject was deemed "rare" and no other effect commenced.
  • Class-D wrote his mother's name, notebook deemed subject as "moderate". Class-D was confused by this and demanded answers.
  • Researcher wrote "Dr. Bright" on paper, the subject was deemed cliche, Dr. Bright suffered the loss of consciousness and does not remember of this experience. Researcher apprehended.
  • Researcher wrote "gravity", no other effect.
  • Researcher entered "Procedure 110-Montauk" on the page, [DATA EXPUNGED] and researcher was demoted to Class-D.

Central narrative:
Just some logs on the SCP, the usual SCP logging of course, along with some interviews with affected persons.

Hook/ Attention Grabber:

A lot of logs regarding the SCP, all effects. Also, this SCP is meta considering that the "cliche-ness" of the subjects is based on how common their appearances are in our writing.

Additional Notes:

got this idea from reading a ton of SCP's and got pissed from the cliches. Pls no cliche


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.content:encoded:
[+] Open

Here's some crit:

a group of reality benders who could 'bless' (call it what you will) chosen areas

Given that reality-benders generally just… bend reality to create and destroy stuff, I think you should further explain your headcanon here.

his curse was the inability to leave the Headquarters and the tombs.

So anyone under the curse is not able to leave the area or what? You make it seem like there are different ways the curse affects people but don't describe them.

Her death caused a chain reaction upon all the members of the group to perish

But why though? Did she willfully kill all of them to take 'em down with her?

Frankly, these people sound more like magic users than reality-benders, considering what they are able to do.

I like the idea, you've got a group of special people banding together to do their own thing. But you don't seem to be doing much with it: why and how do they "bless" places, how is this important to the story? Why is the survivor's curse hyperspecific? Why is the leader called "the Willow"?

The article will include the logs and research created by their group

What is in these logs and what is the research?

This SCP is a man who imbue torture devices with anomalous effects using very specific ingredients. He is presumed to have existed since at least the peak of the Ancient Egyptian empire.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Essentially my concept for an SCP is the above summary, with a document listing a few (not to many don’t worry, it isn’t just an item list facade) of the anomalous devices he is believed to have created. It also features a log of an exploration into a tomb that featured hieroglyphics depicting the man’s anomalous abilities in action. A photograph of him was also discovered, but the church the photograph was located in had been destroyed, and the town soon became suspicious of the foundation agents. The addendum features a mildly successful attempt he made to steal an artifact prior to the foundation’s full understanding of his abilities.

I was suitably spooked out by this tale. The physical description of the deflating creature/guy in the orange coat with the massive smile and the pearly white crooked teeth is very disturbing to picture. Same for the situation with the trucks on the side of the road and the guys yelling and waving. Your redactions also all serve the scary vibe. Where does she work? Why can't she even tell us what it is? Why does she say she went back through twice but only says what happened once?
Characterization of the woman is great, just enough that I can get a sense of who she is. Only thing that I'm not too sure on is the characterization of the husband. Partway through, wife says husband plays the skeptic, but at the end she says that he claims to have seen Bigfoot. Is he a real horror enthusiast for fun's sake, a real believer, or is he a skeptic? Although honestly if you did that intentionally it's probably a good idea because it made the story a little more unsettling.
Thanks for posting.

Hullo! My name is John.

I was introduced to skips maybe three years ago. Since then, I’ve always been coming up with different ideas for them, mostly lost to time. As you can maybe, possibly tell from my username, I especially like the Fifth Church. I also like ARGs, Xx_gaming_xX, and generally mucking about. I’m not much for writing- I’m more of an ideas person- so hopefully the collaborative element of the site will come in if I ever do post anything. I also edit ok.

I would like to say that I’m fire. I can’t. I’m more akin to earth. It’s always there. It supports heavy weights constantly, both the weight of man and the weight of nature, until it can no longer do so. Earth is really just a nice word for dirt. Rocks too, but dirt is at least what first comes to mind for me. It’s rarely the first choice. Fire is exciting and gives off sparks, air is above everything and has a kind of mystical quality to it, water can take exciting and creative forms. Earth is slow-moving. It nurtures and once it’s angry it stays that way, but there’s nothing much to it- at least not to the human eye. look, this ain’t really accurate, it said most representative

It’s a pleasure to introduce myself to y’all!
